My story

I took the long way. It still became my way.

My academic and professional journey was not linear. Over time, however, the different disciplines, countries and organizations I experienced converged into one capability: understanding complex problems from multiple perspectives and turning them into structured action.

Not lost time, but time spent reclaiming direction

I began on a path that was not entirely my own. Moving from life sciences to statistics, and later completing a degree in data science, may look like a series of changes. In retrospect, it was how I learned the way I wanted to understand the world, solve problems and create value.

I did not give up when the path became difficult. I kept rebuilding through research, data, market analysis and project execution. Those experiences gave me a broader analytical perspective and the ability to learn unfamiliar markets and technologies quickly.

From persistence to practical innovation

Working in resource-constrained and fast-moving environments taught me not to wait for a perfect process. I learned to define the workflow myself, coordinate the people involved and build tools that made the work easier to manage.

That mindset carried into every project since—building the process myself when none existed, and turning limited time or resources into something that could hold up under pressure and scale beyond me.

I kept moving through uncertainty.A non-linear path taught me to rebuild, adapt and continue developing my career rather than wait for a perfect route.
I learned by solving unfamiliar problems.Working across life sciences, data, market research and strategy trained me to learn new industries quickly and find the structure behind complex questions.

Claude Skill · Report Quality Control

Reusable Market Research Report QC Skill

Designed a reusable Claude-based quality-control workflow that accepts a PDF report, evaluates it against eight review categories, verifies company information through web research when required, and exports structured issues into Excel.

  • PDF text extraction using Python and pdfplumber.
  • Eight-point QC: language, visuals, numerical consistency, requirements, depth, flow, factual accuracy and company-data accuracy.
  • Severity classification, page-level issue location, suggested correction and source traceability.
  • Excel output with summary, full issue list and category-level tabs using openpyxl.
Reusable Claude QC skill; detailed internal instructions are redacted.
